$comment: Guard for the CHECK-constraint-vs-code-drift bug class.
CHECK constraints. Code kept growing and the constraints did not, so writes
started failing with 23514 — SILENTLY where the caller swallows the error
(createNotification returns false, logActivity caught to console.warn) and
LOUDLY where a route propagates it. Three live examples this file now covers:
chk_notifications_type (4 allowed vs 20 written: the notifications table held
zero rows for its entire history while cron reported notified:4),
chk_ai_activity_action (6 allowed vs 5 more written: ai_activity also held zero
required — every value must exist in the DB CHECK. A missing value is the bug:
the write is rejected, and 3 of 4 call sites so far swallowed it.
legacy   — the DB allows it and no current writer produces it. Rows may already
carry it, so it must never be removed from the constraint without a data check.
declaredIn — files that must literally contain each required value, so this
registry cannot drift from the code it claims to describe.
Anything the DB allows that appears in neither list is reported as a warning,
not a failure: vocabulary creep is normal, undocumented creep is not.

note: 'leads' and 'summary' are deliberately NOT added. They are accepted by the
free-text create route (app/api/tenant/reports/scheduled/route.ts validates
type as z.string().max(50)) and exportEntityFor() silently maps them onto the
contacts export — so a 'leads' report emails a contacts CSV. Adding them would
bless that. The default branch now throws instead; whether to support them
properly is a separate decision.
0050 froze this as ('active','completed','paused','unsubscribed','error') and
the app has always written a sixth value. 'cancelled' is what one-click
unsubscribe, hard-bounce DNC, soft-bounce escalation and the un-enroll button
all set, so every one of those four paths threw 23514 — and because three of
them run inside db.transaction, the contacts.do_not_contact write in the same
transaction rolled back with it: the CRM kept mailing people who opted out.
#2392 moved the un-enroll route's write (and added the contact/sequence
DELETE cancels) into lib/cron/sequence-steps.ts, which is now the third writer.
0120 widens the constraint rather than rewriting the callers, because the
state is real and distinct (see the migration header), and #2392's
cancel-on-delete path needs the same value. The three values no writer
produces are legacy: rows may already carry them.
No migration: the DB was always right. The bug was in code — the zod schema
and the builder offered 'wait', which the constraint never allowed, so every
sequence with a wait step failed on insert. Fixed in lib/api/schemas.ts,
lib/api/schemas/automation.ts and components/tenant/sequence-builder.tsx.
'call' and 'ab_test' are still offered by the builder UI and still rejected
by zod — reported, not fixed.
Regression guard for #35: the UI and zod offered a type the constraint
rejected, which surfaced as a 500 rather than silence.
'sending' is the durable claim of the #2223 outbox flow in the
process-sequences cron: the claim tx flips 'pending' -> 'sending' and
commits BEFORE any SMTP runs, then a second short tx confirms 'sent' or
reverts to 'pending'. A log left 'sending' after a crash is finalised
without resending, so a sequence email can never double-send.
#2258: required is exactly INVOICE_STATUSES (declaredIn) — the DB must
accept every value the API accepts, and the API must accept every value
the DB stores. 'void' was a real product state blocked by the CHECK
(payments + PayU webhook both refuse to pay a void invoice); migration
0112 widened the constraint. 'written_off'/'pending' were DB-legal but
absent from zod, so existing rows were unaddressable via the API; they
were added to INVOICE_STATUSES instead of removed from the DB.
'refunded' — the other zod-only value — was NOT blessed: no code ever
wrote or read invoice status 'refunded' (refunds are ledger entries that
preserve the invoice status, lib/billing/payments.ts:58-59), it read as
a copy-paste from the orders vocabulary, and no row could already carry
it because the CHECK never allowed it. It was removed from zod so the
API answers 400 with the allowed list instead of 23514.
